note: Single source of truth for the literature-derived site data: landform (terrain_morphology) and mineral (mineralogy_tags) labels, site descriptions and Mars water/ice notes. Every label is backed by a verbatim quote from a NASA, USGS or peer-reviewed source published within the last 15 years (or a live NASA mission page), about the site or its footprint region. Labels use a controlled vocabulary (`vocabulary`) so the analog engine's Jaccard comparison never double counts synonyms (gypsum, jarosite -> sulfates; hematite -> iron_oxides; smectite, nontronite -> clays). A row with role "location" carries no label: it shows the cited study was made at the site. Labels with no such source were removed rather than kept on older or generic sources. scripts/apply_site_literature.py writes this into data/earth/candidates.json, data/mars/sites.json and both profile files.

mcmurdo_dry_valleys.description: University Valley, a high-elevation (~1700 m) valley in the Dry Valleys with some of the coldest and driest permafrost soils on Earth: dry permafrost over ice-cemented ground.
known_analog_use: Dry permafrost over ice-cemented ground studied as a Mars analogue (Marinova et al., 2022)

evidence.quote: Some of the coldest and driest permafrost soils on Earth are located in the high-elevation McMurdo Dry Valleys (MDVs) of Antarctica, but little is known about the permafrost microbial communities other than that microorganisms are present in these valleys.

Here, we describe the microbiology and habitable conditions of highly unique dry and ice-cemented permafrost in University Valley, one of the coldest and driest regions in the MDVs (1700 m above sea level; mean temperature −23 °C; no degree days above freezing), where the ice in permafrost originates from vapour deposition rather than liquid water.

haughton_crater.description: Haughton impact structure (Arctic Canada), where gullies formed through the melting of snow and ground ice are studied for their implications for gullies on Mars.
known_analog_use: Gully formation studied as an analogue for Martian gullies (NASA NTRS, LPSC 2020)

evidence.quote: Gully Formation at the Haughton Impact Structure (Arctic Canada) Through the Melting of Snow and Ground Ice, with Implications for Gully Formation on Mars

holuhraun_iceland.description: Lava flow field of the 2014–2015 fissure-fed Holuhraun eruption, with lava–water interactions; a terrestrial analog for volcanic terrains in Elysium Planitia.
known_analog_use: Analog for volcanic terrains in Elysium Planitia (Voigt et al., 2025)
Rover and helicopter mission field test, 2022 (Gwizd et al., 2024)

evidence.quote: The lava flow field covered
The eruption began on a 1.8 km long fissure
This floodplain is largely covered by glacial and fluvial deposits
both locations exhibit polygonal terrain
basaltic fissure eruption at Holuhraun, Iceland

The 2014–2015 Holuhraun eruption in the Icelandic Highland provides a unique opportunity to study a large-volume, fissure-fed eruption—with associated lava–water interactions—that serves as a terrestrial analog for volcanic terrains in Elysium Planitia.

jezero_crater.description: Impact crater holding an ancient river delta where, billions of years ago, a river flowed into a lake; carbonates occur with olivine in the crater and its watershed.
jezero_crater.water_ice_evidence: An ancient river flowed into a lake here, depositing the delta (NASA); no ice reported in the cited sources.

evidence.quote: The delta in Mars’ Jezero Crater is an area where scientists surmise that, billions of years ago, a river once flowed into a lake and deposited rocks and sediments in a fan shape.
We map the position and shape of the olivine 1 μm absorption band and find that carbonates are found in association with olivine which displays a 1 μm band shifted to long wavelengths.

elysium_planitia.description: Smooth plains of impact-fragmented regolith over basaltic lava flows. InSight landing site.

evidence.quote: InSight landed in a degraded impact crater in Elysium Planitia on a smooth sandy, granule- and pebble-rich surface with few rocks
a surface composed of an impact-fragmented regolith overlying basaltic lava flows
a surface composed of an impact-fragmented regolith overlying basaltic lava flows

oxia_planum.description: Plain where many channels emptied into the lowland plains; orbital observations show layers of clay-rich minerals formed in wet conditions about four billion years ago.
oxia_planum.water_ice_evidence: Clay-rich layers formed in wet conditions, likely in a large body of standing water (ESA); no ice reported in the cited sources.

evidence.quote: Oxia Planum lies at the boundary where many channels emptied into the vast lowland plains.
Observations from orbit show that the region exhibits layers of clay-rich minerals that were formed in wet conditions some four billion years ago, likely in a large body of standing water.
Oxia Planum is a clay-bearing site that has preserved evidence of long-term interaction with water during the Noachian era.

utopia_planitia.description: Utopia Planitia, where manganese (hydr)oxides are interpreted as a record of a million-year Hesperian ocean.

evidence.quote: Manganese (Hydr)oxides record the dynamic evolution of a million-year Hesperian Ocean in Utopia Planitia, Mars

chryse_planitia.description: Northern plains where olivine- and pyroxene-bearing materials are exposed by impact craters beneath a sediment-mantled surface.

evidence.quote: Here we combine CRISM L‐detector observations, crater morphology, estimated excavation and structural‐uplift sampling scales, mapped geologic context, and ejecta mobility measurements to reassess crater‐associated olivine and pyroxene exposures across the Chryse Planitia.

Mafic minerals are detected in multiple crater settings, including central structures, crater floors, crater walls, and ejecta blankets, indicating that olivine‐ and pyroxene‐bearing materials are not restricted to a single type of exposure.

meridiani_planum.description: Plains with extensive layered deposits, some rich in hematite, spanning units from the Early Noachian to the Late Amazonian; water-altered bedrock outcrops record past fluid-rock interaction.
meridiani_planum.water_ice_evidence: Water-altered bedrock outcrops record prolonged surface and near-surface fluid/rock interaction (Hynek & Di Achille, 2017); no ice reported in the cited sources.

evidence.quote: this area contains extensive layered deposits, some of which are rich in the mineral hematite
this area contains extensive layered deposits, some of which are rich in the mineral hematite

amazonis_arcadia_ap8.description: Candidate landing site AP-8 on the boundary between Arcadia and northern Amazonis Planitia, in the northern mid-latitudes; mapped thermal contraction polygons point to ice tens of centimetres below the surface.
amazonis_arcadia_ap8.water_ice_evidence: Near-surface excess ice: ice beneath the mapped polygons is estimated at tens of cm depth (Luzzi et al., 2025).

evidence.quote: We have mapped and measured ∼9,000 thermal contraction polygons.
We estimate ice beneath these polygons to be on the order of tens of cm from the surface, which is sufficiently shallow to be accessible for potential in situ resource utilization (ISRU).

planum_boreum.description: The north polar ice cap: about 2 km of layered ice, sand and dust (the north polar layered deposits) above an ice-sand basal unit, estimated at about 4 million years old.
planum_boreum.water_ice_evidence: Massive water ice: radar shows thick ice-and-dust layers separated by layers of nearly pure ice (NASA PIA10652).

evidence.quote: The North Polar Layered Deposits (NPLD) of Mars are ice‐rich sedimentary layers that formed under the influence of Mars' modern climate and thus record the recent climatic history of Mars, analogous to terrestrial ice sheets.
The radar image reveals four never-before-seen thick layers of ice and dust separated by layers of nearly pure ice.

We find significant glass as well as diverse crystalline minerals, which suggests that surface processes like impacts and volcanism were active during the late Amazonian and transported sediments from across the planet to the north pole.

planum_australe.description: The south polar cap: a water ice-rich polar cap with a permanent carbon dioxide ice cap; the Mars Polar Lander site lies about 2.4 km high, midway into the polar layered terrain.
planum_australe.water_ice_evidence: Water ice-rich south polar cap (NASA PIA26773).

evidence.quote: This is the highest-resolution view of the water ice-rich south polar cap of Mars captured by NASA’s Psyche mission after it made its close approach with the planet for a gravity assist.

mawrth_vallis.description: Mawrth Vallis region with a large 25 km impact crater; light-toned clays rich in iron, magnesium and aluminium, some 200 m deep in places, under darker caps thought to be volcanic.
mawrth_vallis.water_ice_evidence: Liquid water ran through Mawrth Vallis about 3.6 billion years ago (ESA Mars Express); no modern ice reported in the cited sources.

evidence.quote: It is also older and more weathered, and is dominated by a large 25 km-wide impact crater with a partly collapsed wall and a smaller crater inside at its central point (a central pit).
Alongside HRSC, Mars Express has employed its spectrometer (OMEGA) to identify the clay minerals seen here, finding them to be rich in iron, magnesium and aluminium.

noctis_labyrinthus.description: Many depressions in Noctis Labyrinthus contain water-bearing minerals, suggesting persistent water during the Late Hesperian to Amazonian.
noctis_labyrinthus.water_ice_evidence: Water-bearing minerals in many depressions, suggesting water was available during the Late Hesperian to Amazonian (NASA PIA18632).

evidence.quote: Many of the depressions in Noctis Labyrinthus contain water-bearing minerals, suggesting that water was available and persistent in this region during the Late Hesperian to Amazonian epochs on Mars, a time when the climate is believed to have been dry and cold like we see today.

hebrus_valles.description: Channel system in the northern lowlands west of the Elysium volcanic region, with deep pits that may be cave entrances in carbonate- and sulfate-rich rock.
hebrus_valles.water_ice_evidence: Pits might retain subsurface water ice (HiRISE ESP_048036_2025); GRS data show elevated water-equivalent hydrogen (Sharma et al., 2025).

evidence.quote: Hebrus Valles are a complex set of channels in the northern lowlands of Mars just to the west of the Elysium volcanic region.
The channel system is thought to be early Amazonian in age (as far back as 3 billion years ago), which is younger than many of the other outflow channels on Mars.
TES data reveal enrichment in carbonates and sulfates near the skylights, and GRS data show elevated water-equivalent hydrogen.

huygens_crater.description: Large double-ring impact crater, about 470 km across, in the heavily cratered southern highlands.

evidence.quote: Captured by the multispectral imager instrument on NASA’s Psyche mission, this is an enhanced-color view of the large double-ring crater Huygens (upper right; about 290 miles, or 470 kilometers, in diameter) and the surrounding heavily cratered southern highlands near 15 degrees south latitude.

columbus_crater.description: Crater in Terra Sirenum that likely hosted a lake: sulfate deposits overlie clays and ring the crater like a bathtub ring.
columbus_crater.water_ice_evidence: A past lake; sulfates were deposited after the clays as the lake dried out (NASA). No modern ice reported in the cited sources.

evidence.quote: Sulfates are found overlying clay minerals in sediments within Columbus Crater, a depression that likely hosted a lake in the past.
Sulfate salt deposits ring the crater like a bathtub ring and were deposited after the clays, as the lake dried out.
Raman, Mid-IR, and NIR spectroscopic study of calcium sulfates and mapping gypsum abundances in Columbus crater, Mars

deuteronilus_mensae.description: Region of mesas surrounded by lobate debris aprons that radar shows to be composed of nearly pure ice.
deuteronilus_mensae.water_ice_evidence: Lobate debris aprons composed of nearly pure ice (SHARAD radar, NASA PIA12996).

evidence.quote: Recent radar data from the Shallow Radar instrument on the Mars Reconnaissance Orbiter has shown them to be composed of nearly pure ice.

protonilus_mensae.description: Protonilus Mensae, studied for a billion or more years of possible periglacial and glacial cycling.

evidence.quote: A billion or more years of possible periglacial/glacial cycling in Protonilus Mensae, Mars

xanthe_terra_tyras.description: Xanthe Terra, whose sedimentary deposits are discussed for the ancient climate on Mars.
xanthe_terra_tyras.evidence_gap: The only approved Mars source for this site (Hauber et al., 2009) is older than the 15-year literature window, so no landform or mineral labels are given.

summit_station_greenland.description: Summit of the Greenland Ice Sheet. Along the ice-sheet margin, surface melting exposes old ice with a visible stratigraphy of variable dust content.
known_analog_use: Greenland Ice Sheet margin ice studied as an analogue for the north polar layered deposits (Yoldi et al., 2020)

evidence.quote: Along the margin of the Greenland Ice Sheet (GrIS), surface melting exposes a visible stratigraphy with variable dust content.

south_pole_station.description: Amundsen–Scott South Pole Station, Antarctica. No approved source describes this site.
south_pole_station.evidence_gap: The only approved source (ESA, Concordia) describes Concordia Station at Dome C, not the South Pole, so no landform or mineral labels are given.

painted_desert.description: Painted Desert, Arizona, with wide clay-bearing horizons interspersed with iron oxide/hydroxide and carbonate units.
known_analog_use: Field site compared with Mawrth Vallis phyllosilicate and sulfate assemblages (Bishop et al., 2025)

evidence.quote: Pedogenic alteration at the Painted Desert produced wide horizons of clay-bearing units interspersed with units of iron oxides/hydroxides and carbonates.

jaroso_ravine.description: Ravine in the Jaroso hydrothermal system, SE Spain, with extinct iron-rich hydrothermal chimneys studied as Mars analog samples.
known_analog_use: Fossil hydrothermal vent analysed as a Mars analog sample (Demaret et al., 2022)

evidence.quote: In this study, an extinct hydrothermal chimney from the Jaroso hydrothermal system (SE Spain), considered an interesting geodynamic and mineralogical terrestrial analog for Mars, was analyzed using Raman spectroscopy, X-ray diffraction, and scanning electron microscopy coupled with energy dispersive X-ray spectroscopy.

liwa_desert.description: Liwa Desert, United Arab Emirates. Lithified aeolian deposits in the UAE were used as analogues for calcium-sulfate-cemented Martian dunes.
known_analog_use: UAE lithified aeolian deposits used as analogues for the Stimson formation, Gale crater (Krishnamoorthi et al., 2025)

evidence.quote: This research encompasses several key aspects: (a) reconstructing regional and local water flow dynamics in dunes, based on comparison with rover images and terrestrial analogue studies, (b) investigating the SF dunes aquifer system, (c) exploring the calcium sulfate cementation, concretions formation, and organic preservation in SF from analogue studies, and (d) investigating the habitability of water‐saturated zones in dune analogues.

sudbury_impact_structure.description: Sudbury impact structure, Canada, known for the Sudbury Breccia; ranked among terrestrial impact sites used as planetary field analogs.
known_analog_use: Ranked among terrestrial impact sites as field analogs (Lambert & Reimold, 2023)
Robotic sample-return analogue deployment (Moores et al., 2012)

evidence.quote: The so-called Sudbury Breccia occurs in the form of numerous, and sometimes huge/massive, bodies of a melt rock that is thought to be equivalent to the pseudotachylitic breccias of the Vredefort structure ( sic ).

yilgarn_salt_lakes.description: Shallow ephemeral, mildly acidic salt lakes on the Yilgarn Craton, Australia, over paleodrainage channels; their sediments hold halite and gypsum.
known_analog_use: Sediment microbiology of acidic salt lakes as terrestrial analogs to ancient Mars (Aerts et al., 2019)

evidence.quote: The dominant mineral phases in the sediments were quartz, feldspars and amphiboles, while halite and gypsum were the only evaporites detected.

granby_tuff.description: Hydrothermally altered basaltic flows, dikes and tuffs at Granby, Massachusetts, whose Fe-rich vermiculite clays are the best spectral analogy found for the clays of Oxia Planum.
known_analog_use: Spectral analogue for the Fe/Mg clays of Oxia Planum (Krzesińska et al., 2021; Bultel et al., 2022, 2025)

evidence.quote: The Granby formation is represented by basaltic flows, dikes and tuffs, all of which hydrothermally altered.
Amygdales in vesicular basalts are filled with Fe-rich clay and similar Fe-rich clay material, although much more fine-grained is present as dispersed alteration of glass in tuff [6].

Two terrestrial sites were identified and studied: Otago, New Zealand with vermiculitized chlorite-schists that underwent alteration without significant oxidation; and Granby, Massachusetts with basaltic tuffs containing Fe-rich clays of apparent hydrothermal origin filling amygdales.

galena_creek_rock_glacier.description: Ice-cored Galena Creek Rock Glacier, Wyoming, with a boulder debris layer over ice; radar-surveyed to image its internal structure.
known_analog_use: Ground-penetrating radar surveys of ice and debris structure (Petersen et al., 2019; Aguilar et al., 2024)

evidence.quote: The surface debris layer, composed of boulders eroded from headwall bedrock, has been measured at 1–1.5 m thick for the upper section and 2–3 m thick for the lower section (Potter, Reference Potter 1972 ).
The ice-cored Galena Creek Rock Glacier, Wyoming, USA, has been the subject of a number of studies that sought to determine the origin of its ice.

channeled_scablands.description: Flood-carved landscape on the Columbia Plateau, eastern Washington, where megafloods stripped the loess and exposed volcanic basalt.
known_analog_use: Compared with Martian outflow channels such as Ares Vallis (NASA)

evidence.quote: Boulders lie strewn across the landscape, amid towering cliffs and plunging holes.

(The water-filled Snake and Columbia Rivers are much darker by comparison.) Instead, these channels take on a dark color because the overlying loess has been eroded, exposing underlying volcanic basalt.

rio_tinto.description: Río Tinto basin, Spain: an acidic river whose sulfide bioleaching products resemble the sulfate and iron oxide deposits of Mars; a NASA drilling test site.
known_analog_use: Life-detection Mars Analog Project drilling tests (NASA Ames, 2015)

evidence.quote: The similarities between the vast sulfate and iron oxide deposits on Mars and the main sulfide bioleaching products found in the Tinto basin have given Río Tinto the status of a geochemical and mineralogical Mars terrestrial analogue.
Natural Fe-bearing oxides and sulfates from the Rio Tinto Mars analog site

Working in early July at a site at Rio Tinto, Spain — identified as a good analog to certain conditions on Mars — the team used a computerized 35-inch drill to successfully obtain samples from the region’s barren acidic hardened soil.

lake_salda.description: Lake Salda, Turkey: a terrestrial analog for the paleolake in Jezero Crater, hosting active, subfossil and fossil hydromagnesite microbialites.
known_analog_use: Analog for the Jezero Crater paleolake (Gunes et al., 2024)

evidence.quote: ABSTRACT Lake Salda, a terrestrial analog for the paleolake in Jezero Crater on Mars, hosts active, subfossil, and fossil hydromagnesite microbialites, making it an ideal location to study microbialite formation and subsequent processes.

dalangtan_playa.description: Dalangtan saline playa in the hyperarid Qaidam Basin, Tibetan Plateau, with Mars-like salts (magnesium sulfates, chlorides, perchlorates) and polygonal landforms.
known_analog_use: Mars analog site studied since 2008 (Kong et al., 2018)

evidence.quote: Since 2008, we have been studying a saline lake, Dalangtan (DLT) Playa, and its surroundings in a hyperarid region of the Qaidam Basin on the Tibetan Plateau as a potential Mars analog site.

Here we report a terrain characterized by polygons with raised rims, ranging in size from approximately 60 to 120 meters, and exhibiting spatial variation in mineral composition and geometry from the Dalangtan area of the western Qaidam Basin on the Tibetan Plateau.

In addition, salt types similar to those found on Mars, such as magnesium-sulfates, chlorides, and perchlorates, are found at the surface and subsurface in the DLT area (and the other two playas in the Qaidam Basin), thus supporting DLT as a Mars analog in terms of mineralogy and geochemistry.

svalbard_fan_delta.description: Adventdalen fjord-valley, Spitsbergen, whose Holocene fill includes a Gilbert-type delta and permafrost with excess ground ice.

evidence.quote: The fjord‐fill sedimentary succession includes the fjord‐bottom late Weichselian subglacial till of the Last Glacial Maximum, the early Holocene muddy glaciomarine deposits with ice‐rafted debris formed during the fjord deglaciation, and the younger Holocene deposits of a fjord‐head Gilbert‐type delta of which the fluvial distributary plain shows raised alluvial terraces hosting aeolian sedimentation.

The upwards‐grown syngenetic permafrost and the top part of downwards‐grown epigenetic permafrost below contain excess ice in a suite of cryofacies indicating ground‐ice segregation and segregative intrusion.
